conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. I understand you’ve been having worsening abdominal pain near your G-tube site?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been going on for months, but the last two weeks it’s gotten much worse. It’s a dull pain in the upper left side, especially when I’m getting my tube feeds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you mentioned dry heaving too? Any nausea, vomiting, or fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just dry heaving sometimes. No vomiting, no fever. I’ve been worried it’s something serious with the tube or infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked a chest X-ray to make sure there’s no free air, which would suggest a perforation, and it was normal. Your abdomen isn’t distended, and there’s no redness or signs of infection at the G-tube site.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not infected? That’s a relief. But why does it hurt so much now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given your history, the pain is likely related to your known marginal ulcer. Bariatric surgery was consulted and they don’t think you need more imaging or surgery right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had that ulcer problem before. Is it acting up again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s likely an exacerbation. Your labs are normal—no signs of infection or organ issues. We’ll focus on pain control and continue your ulcer medications through the tube.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I got some Dilaudid in the ER and it helped. Will I keep getting that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll manage your pain with IV Dilaudid as needed. Once we’re sure your pain is stable, we’ll switch you to oral oxycodone for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my tube feeds? I’ve been off them because of the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We restarted your continuous tube feeds. You were given D5NS in the ED to prevent low blood sugar, but now that feeds are back on, you should be okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve had those hypoglycemia episodes before. Scary when I pass out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. That’s why we keep the feeds running. We’ll continue your sucralfate and lansoprazole through the tube to protect your stomach lining.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs this morning are stable. Pain seems better? We’re planning to discharge you later today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, much better. Still some ache, but not like before. What should I do when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home on liquid oxycodone for pain as needed. Keep taking your regular meds—rifaximin, sucralfate, lansoprazole, and now we’re adding B12 and multivitamins.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: B12? I didn’t take that before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: After gastric bypass, many patients need B12 supplements. It’s a preventive step. Also, please follow up with pain management—we’d like you to see a specialist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll make the appointment. And my ulcer—should I get checked again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re scheduled for an EGD later this month to check the ulcer. For now, keep the feeds going, take your meds, and call if pain worsens or you develop fever.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you for explaining everything. I feel a lot better knowing it’s not an infection or something torn.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get the discharge papers ready. You should be home within a few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before discharge. Pain still manageable?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve only needed one dose of oxycodone this morning. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Remember: take your meds, keep the feeds running, and follow up with pain clinic and GI. We’ll see you in follow-up soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate all your help.
